name: ENS de Lyon GRADUATE+ Scholarship

universities: École Normale Supérieure de Lyon (ENS de Lyon)

duration: 10 months (one award; M1 or M2 of a master's program)
eligibleNationalities: Open to international (non-European) students with a foreign higher-education degree; no nationality exclusion stated. Bangladeshi nationals eligible.
languageRequirements: Certificate of English and/or French level required depending on discipline and study level (per the ENS de Lyon reference grids; only listed tests are accepted). Exception/waiver if you studied in a French- or English-speaking country or your studies were made entirely in French or English — attach a self-written explanation.
applicationFee: Not stated on the official pages (one application form covers both master's admission and the scholarship)
fundingCovers: Monthly living stipend of €1,000 for 10 months
requiredDocuments: Certificate of diplomas and degrees already obtained (e.g. Bachelor degree); if not in French or English, an officially certified translation
University academic transcript of records; if not in French or English, an officially certified translation
Proof of enrollment for the current year
Additional program-specific documents (may include research projects, language certificates, letters of recommendation); if a document is unavailable, a PDF explanation is expected

timeline.notes: Dates are the official 2026-2027 calendar from the ENS de Lyon application page. As of the 2026-06 anchor this cycle is already CLOSED ('Call for application 2026-2027 is now closed'). The 2027-2028 calendar is stated to be updated in November 2026. The shared deadline above is for the ENS de Lyon-hosted GRADUATE+ programs (CORE, DynLifeSys, MathInfi, PACE all show a 23 January 2026 deadline on graduate-plus.fr); other (non-ENS) GRADUATE+ initiatives on the consortium site have different deadlines.

benefits: Monthly living stipend of €1,000 for 10 months
Funded within the French government's SFRI programme (France 2030, ANR-21-SFRI-0001)
Awarded to the best international students selected for a master's (M1 or M2) in the ENS de Lyon GRADUATE+ initiatives CORE, DynLifeSys, MathInfi, and PACE (PACE is M2 only)
mustKnow: PARTIAL-FUNDING WARNING — this is a monthly LIVING STIPEND only (€1,000/month x 10 months), NOT a full tuition+stipend package. No tuition waiver, travel, or insurance is documented on the official pages; budget for French master's enrollment fees, visa, and living costs beyond the 10 months.

Restricted to four named ENS de Lyon GRADUATE+ initiatives only: CORE (European studies, Advanced Economics), DynLifeSys (Biosciences / Biosciences and modeling of complex systems), MathInfi (mathematics & computer science masters), and PACE (Physics, Astrophysics, Chemistry, Earth — M2 only). You must be selected for one of these masters.

Shorter than the Ampère scholarship: 10 months (vs Ampère's 12 months) and a different funding source (SFRI vs Ampère). Do not confuse the two — a single application form lets you apply for both the master's and the scholarship of excellence.

One combined online form covers BOTH master's admission and the scholarship — there is no separate scholarship application; awards are decided by the ENS de Lyon admission committee. Apply on the correct form for your status (non-European with a foreign degree); applications on the wrong form, by email, or after the deadline are not considered.

GRADUATE+ is a four-university Lyon–Saint-Etienne consortium (Université Claude Bernard Lyon 1, ENS de Lyon, Université Jean Moulin, Université Jean Monnet); this entry covers only the ENS de Lyon-hosted GRADUATE+ initiatives. Other initiatives apply through different routes/sites.

Bangladesh is NOT on the 69-country Campus France/Études en France list, so a Bangladesh-resident applicant uses the direct ENS de Lyon route (the procedure explicitly covers students 'residing in a country not covered by Campus France'), not the CEF/Études en France server.

Language proof (English and/or French, per discipline) is required unless you qualify for the waiver (studied in a French/English-speaking country or studies entirely in French/English) — then attach a self-written explanation.
